title: Green Sea · Winter atmosphere
subtitle: Northern storm passages and continental cold contrast with the southern maritime ridge.
notes: 1 · Northern sea: westerly intervals aid eastward sailing; storms, ridges and cold outbreaks interrupt one another.
2 · Western Gulf and Sembara: intermittent fronts and weaker lows bring rain or snow while the gulf retains relative shelter.
3 · Southern ridge: weaker pressure differences near its axis increase light-wind delays, strongest in January–February.

title: Green Sea · Spring atmosphere
subtitle: Developing land lows open southern and northbound opportunities while northern westerlies remain useful.
notes: 1 · Northern westerly intervals continue into June; cool maritime ridges may interrupt them before the summer reversal.
2 · Southerly flow west of Irrla connects southern westbound legs to the northern corridor; the connection varies with weather.
3 · Maritime inflow reaches Sembara: coastal gray spells, terrain rain and sunny breaks can precede sustained inland warmth.

title: Green Sea · Summer atmosphere
subtitle: A secondary cool northern ridge and Cymean offshore trough supply the July–August westbound season.
notes: 1 · Northern ridge above the offshore trough: recurring E–NE winds, interrupted by disturbances and rain.
2 · Dominant eastern ocean high: southerly flow on its western side; a northbound leg no longer guarantees easy onward sailing to Ursk.
3 · Separate desert heat low: northern-flank easterlies reinforce southern westward flow without making the desert interior rainy.

title: Green Sea · Autumn atmosphere
subtitle: Returning northern disturbances and a southward-retreating ridge create successive sailing opportunities.
notes: 1 · Ursk departures: renewed westerly intervals are useful from mid-September; later autumn brings greater storm exposure.
2 · Southeastern Irrla: eastbound opportunities develop as the ridge retreats south; the timing varies by year.
3 · Dashed arrows: selected southward and southwestward episodes on a ridge’s eastern and southeastern flanks, with waits between legs.
footer: Successive weather opportunities, not one continuous fair-wind route. No permanent Eastern Isles storm belt is assumed.
